newsitem.title: UK: Dlr keeps to narrow ranges in thin European trade.
newsitem.headline: Dlr keeps to narrow ranges in thin European trade.

text.p: The dollar was steady against the mark and yen in morning European trade amid a lack of fresh incentives to push the dollar out of its recent ranges.

Although the dollar ground out another high against the mark in early trade, pushing to its strongest level since February 1994, dealers said this was the result of the recent dollar/mark creep higher.

"Dollar/mark is at the top of its range at the moment and it's been a struggle to get it higher," said Peter Wood, forex trader at Bank of Boston. "There's nothing on the horizon to provide a real catalyst to break these ranges."
Dollar/mark stood at 1.7625/35 at 0800 GMT after its early push to a 41-month high of 1.7665 marks. It traded at 1.7597/07 late Wednesday in Europe.

There was some attention on a Bundesbank news conference expected around 1015 GMT today after its annual out-of-town council meeting in Bavaria. But dealers expect little new to emerge and German rates are seen remaining steady.

The main focus today was the outcome of the two-day Bank of England monetary policy committee meeting with an announcement due at 1100 GMT. Expectations are high the central bank will raise UK interest rates by at least 25 basis points.
These rate expectations, reinforced by strong UK inflation data earlier this week, have been the main factor in sterling's recent gains against the mark to its highest in over six-years.
"Things will be quiet until the announcement, the market is looking for aggressive tightening, anything less than half a point will see sterling lower," said a UK bank dealer.
Sterling/mark was trading at 2.9715/25, just off Wednesday's 73-month peak of 2.9760 marks.
The mark was slightly firmer on its European crosses, particularly the French franc, amid renewed jitters over Europe's monetary union timetable.
French and Italian bond markets gave up some of this week's gains, pressuring the franc and the lira, amid uncertainty over French efforts to qualify for EMU.
A French newspaper report said today the forthcoming audit of French public finances would show the 1997 deficit at 3.6 to 3.7 percent of GDP, above the 3.0 percent EMU reference rate.
Mark/French franc continued Wednesday's climb, trading above 3.38 francs for the first time in nearly four-weeks. By 0830 GMT it stood at 3.3802/07 from 3.3771/76 late Wednesday.
The yen remained steady on the mark and dollar, supported amid ongoing concerns of Japan's rising trade surplus.
With few fresh factors, though, dollar/yen kept to a narrow range between 112.50 and 113.00 yen. By 0830 GMT, it was trading at 112.88/93 from 112.92/97 on Wednesday.
Mark/yen recovered from a fresh 23-month low of 63.75 seen in early trade, ticking back up to 64.00 yen in morning Europe.

There was little on the U.S. data horizon today to shift the dollar out of its ranges apart from the weekly jobless claims data at 1230 GMT. Friday's Friday's June producer prices are the next focus but dealers said the low U.S. inflation outlook is likely to remain low.
